Biology 2009-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2009-II.question: Which one of the following is present in chlorophyll which gives a green colour to plant leaves?
Biology 2009-II.explanation: (b)  Chlorophyll is a tetrapyrrole ring system that contains the magnesium ion. The tetrapyrole ring system chelates magnesium  illustrating a conjugated double bond. This bond gives the light absorption feature to chlorophyll and provides it green colour.

Biology 2009-II.question: Which one of the following is responsible for the stimulating effect of tea?
Biology 2009-II.explanation: (c)  The stimulating nature of  tea is due to alkaloid caffeine found in tea. Caffeine is bitter due to white crystalline xanthine alkaloid. Biology 54

Biology 2009-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2009-II.question: The branches of this tree root themselves like new trees over a large area. The roots then give rise to more trunks and branches. Because of this characteristic and its longevity, this tree is considered immortal and is an integral part of the myths and legends of India. Which tree is this?
Biology 2009-II.explanation: (a)  Banyan (Ficus benghalensis) tree has aerial roots. From the tip of these roots new plant can evolve. In Hinduism, the leaf of the Banyan tree is said to be the place for Lord Krishna.

Biology 2009-II.question: Assertion (A):  The safety air bags fitted in some cars inflate during head-on impact of the car.  Reason (R):  The inflation is due to pumping of air into the balloon during the impact.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of  A
Both  A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A ts true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
Biology 2009-II.answer: Both  A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

Biology 2009-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2009-II.question: Primary source of vitamin-D for human beings is
Biology 2009-II.explanation: (d)  Sun is the primary source of vitamin-D. The body can synthesise vitamin-D itself in presence of sunlight. Vitamin-D is soluble in fat and assists the body to absorb calcium. Its deficiency can cause osteoporosis.

Biology 2009-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2009-II.question: Anaemia is a common health problem especially in women. Which one of the following deficiencies is most frequently responsible for anaemia in India?
Biology 2009-II.explanation: (b)  Iron is the main element in haemoglobin. So its deficiency creates anaemia. Women show careless- ness about their nutrient requirements, so they face the problem generally.

Biology 2009-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2009-II.question: Which one of the following is considered normal blood pressure in man?
Biology 2009-II.explanation: (c)  Systolic pressure in an adult man is 120 mm Hg whereas diastolic pressure is 80 mm Hg normally. High or low blood pressure can create serious conditions in humans.

Biology 2009-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2009-II.question: Anthrax is a disease of human and cattle with a potential for biological warfare. It is caused by
Biology 2009-II.explanation: (a)  Anthrax is an infectious disease occurring by bacteria called Bacillus anthracis. Anthrax spores can be evolved in vitro and used as a biological weapon. Anthrax can’t directly spread from one individual to another but can cause infection through spores.

Biology 2009-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2009-II.question: Which one of the following animals breathe through the skin?
Biology 2009-II.explanation: (c)  Frog takes respiration in water through the moist skin. Whereas on the Earth respiration occurs through lungs Fish has gills, Cockroach has spiracles and pigeon possesses lungs to respire.

Biology 2009-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2009-II.question: For which one among the following diseases vaccine is not yet available?
Biology 2009-II.explanation: (b)  Malaria is a protozoan infection caused by the genus plasmodium in humans. No vaccine is yet available  for this illness.

Biology 2009-II.question: Which one of the following is not a feature of eutrophic lakes?
options: Blooms are frequent in eutrophic lakes
Biology 2009-II.explanation: (c)  Eutrophication is the movement of trophic status of aquatic body (lake, pond) towards the direction of increasing biomass by adding natural or artificial substances. So, its primary productivity is clearly high.

Biology 2009-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2009-II.question: Quinine is a drug used in the treatment of malaria. From which part of the plant it is obtained?
Biology 2009-II.explanation: (c)  Quinine is a natural white crystalline alkaloid. It has antipyretic (fever-reducing), antimalarial, analgesic, and anti-inflammatory qualities. It is present in the bark of cinchona tree.

Biology 2009-II.explanation: (c)  Soyabean oil & seed is a rich source of protein.
